interpretation: Each row is an emulator decision point. hardware_effect=none means configuration/physical identity still differs but a shared emulation implementation is acceptable.

differences.8525: No hardware real-time clock; ports 0xB0-0xBF and 0xE0-0xEF are not RTC decodes.
differences.8530: Battery-backed MM58167-family RTC; registers 16-31 at 0xB0-0xBF and registers 0-15 at 0xE0-0xEF.
differences.required_behavior: Conditional I/O decode, persistent RTC state only for 8530, and correct unsupported/open-bus behavior for 8525.
evidence: model25_techref physical page 258: configuration feature byte says no real-time clock
model30_techref physical pages 38 and 254: RTC I/O ranges and RTC-present feature bit
model30_schematic physical page 6: 58167A-marked device, 32.768 kHz crystal, VBAT
differences.verification: On 8525, INT 15h/C0 feature byte 1 bit 5=0 and RTC I/O does not mutate clock state. On 8530 it is 1 and INT 1Ah get/set/alarm survives emulated power according to battery policy.

differences.8525: IRQ1 sources are keyboard and pointing device.
differences.8530: IRQ1 sources are keyboard, pointing device, and RTC alarm.
differences.required_behavior: Use proprietary shared-source INT 71h dispatch on both; add RTC source and mask/status handling only on 8530.
differences.verification: Keyboard generates the configured normal IRQ1 handler, mouse reaches INT 73h, and only 8530 alarm reaches the RTC alarm path; concurrent pending sources remain distinguishable.

differences.8530: Same XT map as the 8525: 0x81=channel 2, 0x82=channel 3, 0x83=channel 1, 0x87=channel 0. The Model 30 TR Figure 1-8 prints a shifted map (0x80=ch2, 0x81=ch3, 0x82=ch1) that is a documentation error: the 8530 BIOS and diagnostics only ever program the XT addresses, and DMA with buffers above 64 KiB requires the XT decode.
differences.required_behavior: Use one shared XT page-register map for both models. Do NOT implement the Model 30 TR's shifted map: the shared BIOS INT 13h writes the page to 0x81 (FDC/ch2) and 0x82 (HDC/ch3), and under the shifted decode those writes land on the wrong channels, corrupting DMA.
evidence: model25_techref physical page 26, Figure 1-8: XT map
model30_techref physical page 27, Figure 1-8: prints shifted map (0x80=ch2, 0x81=ch3, 0x82=ch1, 0x87=ch0); printed text confirmed at high resolution, but contradicted by the ROMs and live DMA tests
8530 BIOS rev 0 disassembly: FDC/ch2 DMA page -> out 0x81 (F000:1889, 8237 base 0x4); HDC/ch3 DMA page -> out 0x82 (F000:FF5B0, 8237 base 0x6)
8525 BIOS rev 0 disassembly: FDC/ch2 page -> out 0x81 (F000:4B4B); HDC/ch3 page -> out 0x82 (F000:FF5B2)

Live DMA probe (custom boot sector, INT 13h only, buffers at 0x20000/0x30000): XT map lands both FDC and HDD transfers at the intended addresses on both machines; shifted map crashes both (8530 at the first diskette INT 13h, 8525 during POST)
differences.verification: 2026-08-03: custom boot diskette whose boot sector uses only INT 13h to read a diskette sector into 0x20000 and to write/read back an XTA sector at 0x30000. With the emulator's XT map: FDC OK 20000, HDC OK 30000 on both 8525 and 8530. With the Model 30 TR's shifted map wired in temporarily: both machines crash (8530 during the FDC INT 13h, 8525 during POST), confirming the shifted map is not a functional decode. The TR figure's channel-1/2/3 rows are shifted one port while channel 0 stays at 0x87 - an internally inconsistent pattern that marks it as an editing error.

differences.8525: 512 KiB standard upper memory plus optional socketed low 128 KiB, for 640 KiB maximum.
differences.8530: 640 KiB standard; low 128 KiB chips soldered and upper 512 KiB in SIPs.
differences.required_behavior: Expose a 512 KiB 8525 configuration and its port-0x6B remap path. Default 8530 to 640 KiB and do not offer normal absent-low-bank configuration.
differences.verification: 8525 POST boots and reports reduced/remapped memory without the 128 KiB option; both models correctly identify parity bank through port 0x6B bit 7.

differences.8525: ROM model byte 0xFA, INT 15h/C0 submodel 0x01, supplied revision 0x00.
differences.8530: ROM model byte 0xFA, INT 15h/C0 submodel 0x00, supplied revisions 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x04.
differences.required_behavior: Install a coherent model-specific ROM pair and return its table unchanged; model byte alone cannot distinguish the machines.
differences.verification: Read physical 0xFFFFE and call INT 15h/C0. Assert common 0xFA model byte and distinct submodel/feature values.

differences.8525: INT 15h/C0 feature byte 1 bit 5 is clear.
differences.8530: INT 15h/C0 feature byte 1 bit 5 is set.
differences.required_behavior: Do not fabricate an RTC on 8525 to satisfy generic PC expectations.
differences.verification: Diagnostic date/time utilities choose their model-specific paths and the 8525 utility's no-RTC fallback remains reachable.

differences.8525: Two 62-pin 8-bit I/O-channel slots on a riser.
differences.8530: Three 62-pin 8-bit I/O-channel slots on a riser.
differences.required_behavior: Limit configured expansion adapters to the physical slot count if the emulator exposes slots; electrical adapter model can be shared.
differences.verification: Machine configuration UI/API exposes two versus three assignable slots.

differences.8525: Integrated 12-inch monochrome or color analog display through a 14-pin planar connector.
differences.8530: Separate analog monitor through external 15-pin D-sub with monitor-sense 0/1.
differences.required_behavior: Model integrated monitor identity separately from external monitor sense; MCGA core can be shared.
differences.verification: 8525 monochrome/color variants and 8530 8503/color monitor selections produce their correct sense results and grayscale behavior.

differences.8525: Single system/display enclosure; one 12-pin power connector; planar earphone connection.
differences.8530: Separate system unit/monitor; two 6-pin power connectors; RTC VBAT wiring.
differences.required_behavior: Only VBAT/RTC persistence has software-visible impact; retain the rest as machine metadata.
differences.verification: Machine metadata and RTC battery controls match profile.

differences.8525: 1987 launch machines were diskette configurations; IBM added optional no-slot or adapter-based 20 MB drive in 1988.
differences.8530: Launch 8530-021 included one 20 MB integrated-controller fixed disk; 8530-002 used two diskette drives.
differences.required_behavior: Default configurations differ even though the 0x320-0x32F, IRQ5, DMA3, 44-pin planar interface is common.
differences.verification: Port 0x62 bit 2 and port 0x65 bit 0 reflect installed/disabled drive state in every configuration.

differences.8525: One 720 KiB drive standard; second 720 KiB drive optional.
differences.8530: 8530-002 has two 720 KiB drives; 8530-021 has one 720 KiB drive plus fixed disk.
differences.required_behavior: Set BIOS equipment/configuration and DOR drive-presence behavior from selected machine configuration.
differences.verification: POST and starter disk report the expected drive count.

differences.8525: Two supplied planar pairs, Type 1 00F2092/00F2093 and Type 2 00F2122/00F2123; combined images differ by only 10 bytes in five runs but must stay paired with the selected planar.
differences.required_behavior: Offer explicit ROM revision/planar selection; interleave even chip at offsets 0,2,... and odd chip at 1,3,... into F0000-FFFFF.
differences.verification: Every built 64 KiB image has byte-sum modulo 256 equal to zero, reset vector at 0xFFF0, 0xFA at 0xFFFE, and expected date at 0xFFF5.

differences.8525: Starter 1.00 and advanced diagnostics 1.00; date/time utility contains no-RTC feature handling.
differences.8530: Starter 1.02 and advanced diagnostics 1.05; direct RTC service usage and larger model-specific fixed-disk diagnostic.
differences.required_behavior: Use each model's own images for validation. Passing only one model's disk is insufficient evidence for the other.
differences.verification: Boot and execute the CPU/I/O, date/time, diskette, fixed-disk, keyboard/mouse, serial, parallel, and display diagnostics from the matching image.
